def: The new policy's probability of a sampled token divided by the old policy's, used to reweight old samples and equal to 1 when nothing has changed.
A stand-in objective, the ratio times the advantage, that can be optimised on data from an older policy and matches the policy gradient at the starting point.
Rewriting an expectation under one distribution as an expectation under another by weighting each sample by the ratio of their probabilities.
The neighbourhood of the current policy, usually defined by a KL limit, within which a local approximation of the objective is trusted.
PPO's objective min(rA, clip(r, 1-eps, 1+eps)A), which stops a token earning more credit once its probability has moved eps in the helpful direction.
Learning only from data generated by the current (or almost current) policy, so each batch of rollouts is discarded after a few updates.
A frozen copy of the model a run started from, usually the SFT model, against which the tuned policy's drift is measured and penalised.
A cost proportional to the KL divergence between the tuned policy and the reference, applied per token in RLHF to keep the model close to where the reward model is reliable.
Three single-sample estimators of KL divergence: k1 is unbiased but noisy and can be negative, k2 is biased, and k3 is unbiased and never negative.
The effect where pushing a policy to maximise a learned reward raises the reward score while true quality peaks and then declines.
A rule that raises or lowers the KL coefficient during training so that the measured KL stays near a target value.
The share of tokens whose probability ratio left the clip range in a PPO update, a diagnostic for how far each iteration moves the policy.
